item.text:
**6B.2 | Tinubu in 2024**
Bottom line: **mixed, leaning negative on realized access, with real but uneven welfare-oriented policy intent.** Tinubu’s 2024 record includes several concrete moves toward education, social protection, conflict resettlement, and targeted relief, but the clearest outcome evidence still shows severe food insecurity, cost-of-living pressure, and persistent gaps in child safety and reintegration. I found little direct 2024 evidence of broad, measurable gains in water, sanitation, or housing access.

**Accepted claims**
- **President Tinubu Directs Expeditious Processing of Welfare Benefits, Demands Monthly KPI Reports** | State House | 2024-02-22 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-expeditious-processing-of-welfare-benefits-demands-monthly-kpi-reports/  
  Tinubu explicitly ordered faster processing of welfare benefits and monthly reporting, which is direct evidence of trying to improve social protection delivery for vulnerable citizens.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.9

- **With Good Governance and Commitment, We Must Overcome Old Subsidy Beneficiaries** | State House | 2024-03-15 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/with-good-governance-and-commitment-we-must-overcomee-old-subsidy-benificiaries-president-tinubu/  
  Tinubu tied subsidy reform to student loans, consumer credit, and social welfare, and said relief should be targeted with NIN data. This is strong evidence of a policy design aimed at expanding access to basic opportunity and protection rather than pure patronage.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.10

- **In Detail: The Student Loan (Access to Higher Education) Act, 2024** | State House | 2024-04-04 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/in-detail-the-student-loan-access-to-higher-education-act-2024/  
  The presidency framed the student-loan system as a way to expand access to higher education and build human capital for lower-income families. That is direct education-access evidence.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8

- **President Tinubu Approves Takeoff of Consumer Credit Scheme** | State House | 2024-04-24 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-approves-takeoff-of-consumer-credit-scheme/  
  Tinubu presented consumer credit as a way to improve quality of life and social mobility by helping people finance homes, vehicles, education, and healthcare. This is indirect but real evidence for broader access to basic welfare goods.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8

- **President Tinubu Launches National Resettlement Scheme For Conflict Victims** | State House | 2024-07-06 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-launches-national-resettlement-scheme-for-conflict-victims/  
  The administration launched a resettlement scheme for displaced and conflict-affected communities, explicitly framing it as rehabilitation and reintegration. This is one of the clearest direct welfare-access items in the record, especially for housing and displacement-related needs.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **President Tinubu Launches Education Campaign, Sys no Child Should be Excluded from Learning** | State House | 2024-05-13 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-launches-education-campaign-sys-no-child-should-be-excluded-from-learning/  
  Tinubu backed girls’ education, anti-GBV policy, and inclusive schooling, which supports access to basic education for girls and children. This is mostly programmatic rhetoric, but it is still concrete welfare-oriented policy language.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8

- **President Tinubu Offers Scholarships, Housing to Families of Slain Soldiers** | State House | 2024-03-27 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-offers-scholarships-housing-to-families-of-slain-soldiers/  
  Tinubu ordered scholarships and housing support for families of slain soldiers and pushed rapid payment of benefits. This is direct, if narrow, evidence of material support for households facing severe loss.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **Supporting Nigeria’s Homegrown Reforms: New World Bank Financing for Inclusive Growth and Revenue Diversification** | World Bank | 2024-06-13 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/13/supporting-nigeria-homegrown-reforms-new-world-bank-financing-for-inclusive-growth-and-revenue-diversification  
  The World Bank said the reform package was meant to create fiscal space for public services and scale up support to vulnerable households. It also explicitly tied the program to inclusive growth, which is the strongest external validation of a welfare-oriented policy direction.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9, 5B.10

- **World Bank Approves New Financing for Nigeria to Improve Health Outcomes, Safety of Dams and Irrigation Services** | World Bank | 2024-09-26 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/09/26/world-bank-approves-new-financing-for-nigeria-to-improve-health-outcomes-safety-of-dams-and-irrigation-services  
  This package targeted health, basic education governance, and irrigation/hydropower resilience. That is the best direct evidence I found for improvements in service-delivery systems touching health, education, and water-adjacent infrastructure.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8

- **Nigeria Development Update, October 2024** | World Bank | 2024-10-17 | https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099524010162440675  
  The World Bank said reforms were starting to improve inflation, fiscal position, and reserves, but it also stressed continued pain and incomplete execution. That makes this a qualified positive for future access, not proof of broad 2024 gains.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.2, 5B.9, 5B.10

**Negative / limiting evidence**
- **Nigeria: 10 Years After Chibok, Schoolchildren Still at Risk** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-04-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/11/nigeria-10-years-after-chibok-schoolchildren-still-risk  
  HRW said authorities had failed to sustain safe-learning measures, leaving schoolchildren at continuing risk. That undercuts any claim that access to education became materially safer in 2024.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.9

- **Nigeria: Girls Failed by Authorities After Escaping Boko Haram Captivity** | Amnesty International | 2024-06-09 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/nigeria-girls-failed-by-authorities-after-escaping-boko-haram-captivity-new-report/  
  Amnesty documented unlawful detention and weak reintegration support for girls and young women escaping Boko Haram captivity. This is strong evidence against effective access to protection and reintegration for vulnerable survivors.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **At least 3 killed in Nigeria at protests over high cost of living** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-01 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/hundreds-gather-across-nigerian-cities-to-protest-cost-of-living-crisis-3548376  
  Reuters linked the protests to subsidy removal, naira devaluation, electricity tariff hikes, and inflation above 34%. That is strong evidence that access to basic goods and services was deteriorating for many households.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.2, 5B.9, 5B.10, 5B.8

- **Insecurity, rising costs push 31 million Nigerians into acute food shortage, study says** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-27 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/insecurity-rising-costs-push-31-million-nigerians-into-acute-food-shortage-study-says-3589474  
  The Reuters report said 31.8 million Nigerians were acutely food insecure, with subsidy removal and insecurity among the drivers. This is the clearest negative evidence against improved food security in 2024.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.2, 5B.9, 5B.10, 5B.8

- **Nigeria police used excessive force to violently quash #EndBadGovernance protests** | Amnesty International | 2024-11-28 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/nigeria-police-used-excessive-force-to-violently-quash-endbadgovernance-protests/  
  Amnesty said police killed at least 24 protesters and detained more than 1,200 during protests over economic hardship and corruption. This shows that welfare grievances were met with coercion rather than a welfare-first response.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.9, 5B.8, 3B.4

- **4 Nigerian journalists charged with cybercrime, defamation over fraud investigation** | CPJ | 2024-02-09 | https://cpj.org/2024/02/4-nigerian-journalists-charged-with-cybercrime-defamation-over-fraud-investigation/  
  Criminal charges against journalists investigating corruption weaken oversight of who gets access to public resources and who is being left behind. This is indirect, but it undercuts a genuine welfare-first governance model.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.7, 5B.8

- **Nigeria police charge 4 journalists with cybercrimes for corruption reporting** | CPJ | 2024-10-03 | https://cpj.org/2024/10/nigeria-police-charge-4-journalists-with-cybercrimes-for-corruption-reporting/  
  Continued use of cybercrime charges against journalists suggests a punitive information environment, which makes it harder to monitor whether welfare programs are actually reaching people.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.7, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **Tinubu under fire for appointing son-in-law head of housing agency** | BusinessDay | 2024-02-21 | https://businessday.ng/news/article/tinubu-under-fire-for-appointing-son-in-law-head-of-housing-agency/  
  The son-in-law appointment to the Federal Housing Authority is a concrete nepotism signal. It weakens the claim that housing and related welfare institutions were insulated from patronage.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8

- **President Tinubu: I have no Cabal or Sponsors to Compensate** | State House | 2024-07-26 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-i-have-no-cabal-or-sponsors-to-compensate/  
  Tinubu denied patronage politics while emphasizing social support, but this remains rhetoric and does not by itself demonstrate improved access. It is useful mainly as counterbalance to the nepotism critique.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8

**Search gap**
- I found **strong direct evidence for education and social protection**, some evidence for **health** and **food security**, and weaker, more indirect evidence for **housing**.
- I found **very little direct 2024 evidence on sanitation or household water access**. The closest material was World Bank-backed work on dams, irrigation, and resilience, which is relevant but not the same as improved access to safe water/sanitation at household level.
- So the best calibrated conclusion is: **Tinubu clearly expanded or promised several welfare-access channels in 2024, but the evidence of broad on-the-ground improvement in basic services is still limited, and food/education protection problems remained severe.**
